who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane: task watchdog over every task, int-1112
what: A test parked on thread::park ran 10 hours: the test queue judges a running test only by its wall-clock timeout. The task watchdog's core (blaze_profile::stuck::Watch) can judge a test by its CPU and its output, but the queue learns neither while a test runs: the fork server answers once, at the test's end, with its whole output, and never says the forked child's pid, so no one can read the child's CPU clock.
cost: a quiet test is caught only at its timeout, never named with its stacks or last output while it hangs
cause: the wire protocol has no frame for a started child (its pid) and no streamed output; the queue is sans-IO with only Run/Ended/Kill
class: a watched process whose progress signals never reach its watcher
prevention: a Frame::Started { id, pid } from the fork server and output streamed in chunks (Frame::Output { id, bytes }); the queue keeps a Watch, a TaskSeen per running attempt (Task::Child(pid), span = output bytes seen, cpu from the driver's child_cpu_ns), a Due::Look on its wheel each LOOK_EVERY, a per-test quiet bound (Job::quiet, default 300 s, overridable as the timeout is) and Failure::Stuck naming the test with its last output
